name: Pedaiah
overview: Pedaiah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Kolaiah. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes elaborating on his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Pedaiah means 'Yahweh ransoms,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's redemptive work. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:7, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Pedaiah as the son of Kolaiah and infers Joed as his father. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Though Pedaiah's role in the biblical narrative is limited, his inclusion in the genealogical records of Nehemiah underscores the continuity of the Benjaminite lineage during the post-exilic period. His mention helps affirm the restoration and reestablishment of the tribes of Israel, reflecting God's faithfulness in preserving His covenant people.
